Extended diameter is the supremum of pairwise extended distances, with empty diameter zero. Conversion to real diameter is explicitly guarded by finiteness; metric edistance is distinguished from distance.
ofReal truncates a real value below at zero; toReal has its finite-value meaning and the separate infinity convention. These total constructions grant no finiteness.
The full natural-indexed cover infimum, scale restriction, extended sum and nonemptiness guard match the exact basis header. Infimum of an empty cover family is specified, so no existence is assumed.

H is explicitly native mkMetric with gauge r↦r^u and no dimensional normalization. Its cover evaluation is a selected theorem M001, not an extra definition-granted premise; arbitrary subsets are permitted.

dimH is the supremum of nonnegative finite exponents whose native Hausdorff measure is infinite, in ENNReal with empty supremum zero. Borelization and the extended codomain match the pinned definition; critical-exponent facts remain M inputs.
The unit interval is the closed real interval [0,1], including both endpoints, and matches unitInterval in the exact basis header.

The intermediate product has the specified maximum metric and Borel structure; no Euclidean metric is silently assigned to it. B×I is unambiguous in the intermediate lemmas, with metric change exported by N106.

Coordinate concatenation is a total map from the maximum product to the Euclidean (m+1)-space and matches Fin.lastCases in the header, including m=0. The identification of the target set is explicit; bijectivity and metric bounds are internal claims N106.
volume is ordinary Lebesgue measure on ℝ with Borel structure and evaluation on arbitrary sets. This does not assume measurability of projections or covering sets.
The constant indicator is a total ENNReal-valued function for every subset and constant, including infinity. Its definition does not assume measurability or involve undefined subtraction.

The lower integral is defined for arbitrary ENNReal-valued functions by measurable simple minorants; its finite-range integral uses value times measure. No integrability or finiteness is assumed; series interchange remains M014.

LipschitzWith is the full pairwise extended-distance inequality with a finite nonnegative constant; the usual metric interpretation has the same meaning. No continuity theorem is granted by naming it.
AntilipschitzWith is the reverse pairwise extended-distance inequality with a finite nonnegative constant. Its actual use on metric/extended metric spaces agrees with the native source conditions.

The closed segment is the set of nonnegative affine combinations with coefficients summing to one. Scalar/vector domains and all coefficient conditions are explicit; segment identification is separately supplied by M013.
finrank has its finite-dimensional meaning and the native total zero convention in infinite rank. Every proof use is in a finite-dimensional space, whose hypotheses remain explicit in M009–M012.
